notes: As a describing word: ruso, rusa (Russian).

sentences.text: El ruso usa otras letras.
sentences.translation: Russian uses different letters.

sentences.text: Mi vecina es de Moscú y me enseña ruso.
sentences.translation: My neighbour is from Moscow and teaches me Russian.

sentences.text: El libro está escrito en ruso.
sentences.translation: The book is written in Russian.

sentences.text: Los niños se pusieron en círculo.
sentences.translation: The children got into a circle.

sentences.text: La luna llena parece un círculo perfecto.
sentences.translation: The full moon looks like a perfect circle.

sentences.text: Estamos dando vueltas en círculos.
sentences.translation: We're going round in circles.

notes: grito is also 'I shout', from gritar.

sentences.text: Oímos gritos en el piso de al lado.
sentences.translation: We heard shouting in the flat next door.

sentences.text: ¿De quién era ese grito?
sentences.translation: Whose scream was that?

sentences.text: A las tres me despertó un grito.
sentences.translation: A scream woke me up at three.

sentences.text: Subo en ascensor, que estoy cansada.
sentences.translation: I'm taking the lift up, I'm tired.

sentences.text: Mi edificio no tiene ascensor.
sentences.translation: My building doesn't have a lift.

sentences.text: En este hotel hay cuatro ascensores.
sentences.translation: There are four lifts in this hotel.

sentences.text: Un helicóptero pasó por encima de casa.
sentences.translation: A helicopter flew over our house.

sentences.text: ¿Has volado alguna vez en helicóptero?
sentences.translation: Have you ever flown in a helicopter?

sentences.text: Toda la noche hubo helicópteros sobre la ciudad.
sentences.translation: There were helicopters over the city all night.

notes: estar obligado a + verb = to be obliged to do something.

sentences.text: No estás obligado a venir.
sentences.translation: You're not obliged to come.

sentences.text: Nos vimos obligados a vender la casa.
sentences.translation: We were forced to sell the house.

sentences.text: Se sintió obligada a ayudar.
sentences.translation: She felt obliged to help.

gloss: to hand over, to hand in; to deliver

sentences.text: Mañana entrego el informe a mi jefa.
sentences.translation: Tomorrow I'm handing the report in to my boss.

sentences.text: Ya entregué el examen.
sentences.translation: I've already handed in my exam.

sentences.text: El cartero entregó el paquete a mi vecina.
sentences.translation: The postman delivered the parcel to my neighbour.

sentences.text: Entregue esta carta en mano, por favor.
sentences.translation: Please deliver this letter by hand.

sentences.text: Los bomberos encontraron un escape de gas.
sentences.translation: The firefighters found a gas leak.

sentences.text: Su plan de escape salió mal.
sentences.translation: Their escape plan went wrong.

sentences.text: Hemos tenido dos escapes de agua este año.
sentences.translation: We've had two water leaks this year.

sentences.text: Esta tarde hacemos limpieza general.
sentences.translation: This afternoon we're doing a big clean.

sentences.text: Trabaja en la limpieza de oficinas.
sentences.translation: She works cleaning offices.

sentences.text: Hacer la limpieza del piso me lleva toda la mañana.
sentences.translation: Cleaning the flat takes me all morning.

notes: Often just means 'excellent': ¡Magnífico! = Great!

sentences.text: Has hecho un trabajo magnífico.
sentences.translation: You've done a superb job.

sentences.text: Por dentro, la iglesia es magnífica.
sentences.translation: Inside, the church is magnificent.

sentences.text: Mi profesora de piano era magnífica.
sentences.translation: My piano teacher was superb.

gloss: worker (often in a factory, on a farm or a building site)
notes: As a describing word, trabajador means hard-working.

sentences.text: Hoy los trabajadores del metro están en huelga.
sentences.translation: The underground workers are on strike today.

sentences.text: Mi abuelo fue trabajador del campo toda su vida.
sentences.translation: My grandfather was a farm worker all his life.

sentences.text: Las trabajadoras de la limpieza ganan muy poco.
sentences.translation: Cleaning workers earn very little.

sentences.text: Mi abuela tuvo una caída en la escalera.
sentences.translation: My grandmother had a fall on the stairs.

sentences.text: Desde aquí hay una caída de cien metros.
sentences.translation: From here there's a hundred-metre drop.

sentences.text: Las caídas son peligrosas para los mayores.
sentences.translation: Falls are dangerous for older people.

sentences.text: Mañana van a bajar las temperaturas.
sentences.translation: Temperatures are going to drop tomorrow.

sentences.text: ¿A qué temperatura pongo el horno?
sentences.translation: What temperature should I set the oven to?

sentences.text: La temperatura del agua es perfecta.
sentences.translation: The water temperature is perfect.

notes: hacer ejercicio = to exercise.

sentences.text: Hago ejercicio antes de desayunar.
sentences.translation: I exercise before breakfast.

sentences.text: El médico dice que necesito más ejercicio.
sentences.translation: The doctor says I need more exercise.

sentences.text: Haced los ejercicios de la página diez.
sentences.translation: Do the exercises on page ten.

sentences.text: Los perros son famosos por su lealtad.
sentences.translation: Dogs are famous for their loyalty.

sentences.text: Para él, la lealtad a la familia es lo primero.
sentences.translation: For him, loyalty to family comes first.

sentences.text: Con dinero no se compra la lealtad.
sentences.translation: Loyalty can't be bought with money.

notes: It is feminine but takes el in the singular: el ala, las alas.

sentences.text: El pájaro tiene un ala rota.
sentences.translation: The bird has a broken wing.

sentences.text: Las gallinas tienen alas, pero casi no vuelan.
sentences.translation: Hens have wings, but they can hardly fly.

sentences.text: Desde mi asiento solo veo el ala del avión.
sentences.translation: From my seat I can only see the plane's wing.

sentences.text: Ya hemos mandado las invitaciones de la boda.
sentences.translation: We've already sent out the wedding invitations.

sentences.text: Lo siento, no puedo aceptar tu invitación.
sentences.translation: I'm sorry, I can't accept your invitation.

sentences.text: Fui a la fiesta sin invitación.
sentences.translation: I went to the party without an invitation.

sentences.text: El anillo lleva un diamante pequeño.
sentences.translation: The ring has a small diamond.

sentences.text: Le regaló unos pendientes de diamantes.
sentences.translation: He gave her diamond earrings.

sentences.text: Nadie sabe quién robó el diamante.
sentences.translation: Nobody knows who stole the diamond.

sentences.text: Según la leyenda, el lago no tiene fondo.
sentences.translation: According to the legend, the lake has no bottom.

sentences.text: Hay muchas leyendas sobre este castillo.
sentences.translation: There are many legends about this castle.

sentences.text: Ese jugador es una leyenda del fútbol.
sentences.translation: That player is a football legend.

sentences.text: Esta playa es un paraíso.
sentences.translation: This beach is paradise.

sentences.text: La Biblia dice que el paraíso era un jardín.
sentences.translation: The Bible says that paradise was a garden.

sentences.text: Para un niño, una tienda de juguetes es el paraíso.
sentences.translation: For a child, a toy shop is paradise.

notes: de costumbre = usual: como de costumbre = as usual.

sentences.text: Tengo la costumbre de leer antes de dormir.
sentences.translation: I'm in the habit of reading before I go to sleep.

sentences.text: Aquí es costumbre saludar con dos besos.
sentences.translation: Here it's the custom to greet people with two kisses.

sentences.text: Mi abuelo tiene costumbres muy raras.
sentences.translation: My grandfather has some very odd habits.

sentences.text: Pasamos el fin de semana en una cabaña de madera.
sentences.translation: We spent the weekend in a wooden cabin.

sentences.text: Los niños hicieron una cabaña con ramas.
sentences.translation: The children built a hut out of branches.

sentences.text: Las cabañas junto al río tienen baño.
sentences.translation: The cabins by the river have a bathroom.

sentences.text: Déjale el mensaje a mi secretaria.
sentences.translation: Leave the message with my secretary.

sentences.text: Mi tío fue secretario del alcalde.
sentences.translation: My uncle was the mayor's secretary.

sentences.text: La secretaria me dio cita para el lunes.
sentences.translation: The secretary gave me an appointment for Monday.

gloss: slowly, gradually (a bit more formal than despacio)
notes: In everyday speech, despacio is more common: habla despacio.

sentences.text: El médico nos habló clara y lentamente.
sentences.translation: The doctor spoke to us clearly and slowly.

sentences.text: Lentamente, la ciudad volvió a la normalidad.
sentences.translation: Gradually, the city went back to normal.

sentences.text: Por la lluvia, el río sube lentamente.
sentences.translation: Because of the rain, the river is gradually rising.

sentences.text: Hoy es el último ensayo antes del concierto.
sentences.translation: Today is the last rehearsal before the concert.

sentences.text: Tengo que escribir un ensayo sobre la guerra.
sentences.translation: I have to write an essay about the war.

sentences.text: En el teatro, los ensayos son muy largos.
sentences.translation: At the theatre, rehearsals are very long.

sentences.text: Me he hecho socio de un gimnasio.
sentences.translation: I've joined a gym.

sentences.text: El gimnasio abre a las seis de la mañana.
sentences.translation: The gym opens at six in the morning.

sentences.text: Algunos gimnasios abren toda la noche.
sentences.translation: Some gyms are open all night.

sentences.text: Esta noche estaremos a cinco grados negativos.
sentences.translation: Tonight it'll be five degrees below zero.

sentences.text: No seas tan negativa, todo va a salir bien.
sentences.translation: Don't be so negative, it's all going to be fine.

sentences.text: El hotel tiene muchos comentarios negativos.
sentences.translation: The hotel has a lot of negative reviews.

gloss: language (a way of speaking or communicating)
notes: For the language of a country, Spanish says idioma or lengua.

sentences.text: ¡Cuidado con ese lenguaje!
sentences.translation: Watch your language!

sentences.text: Los médicos usan un lenguaje difícil.
sentences.translation: Doctors use difficult language.

sentences.text: El lenguaje del cuerpo dice mucho.
sentences.translation: Body language says a lot.

sentences.text: El coche nuevo no cabe en el garaje.
sentences.translation: The new car doesn't fit in the garage.

sentences.text: Tenemos una plaza de garaje cerca de casa.
sentences.translation: We have a parking space in a garage near home.

sentences.text: Mi vecino tiene dos garajes y un solo coche.
sentences.translation: My neighbour has two garages and only one car.

sentences.text: Mi perro siempre trae el palo.
sentences.translation: My dog always brings back the stick.

sentences.text: El niño escribe su nombre en la arena con un palo.
sentences.translation: The boy is writing his name in the sand with a stick.

sentences.text: Recoge palos para el fuego.
sentences.translation: Collect sticks for the fire.

sentences.text: El león es el rey de la selva.
sentences.translation: The lion is the king of the jungle.

sentences.text: Mis hijos son valientes como leones.
sentences.translation: My children are as brave as lions.

sentences.text: La leona protege a sus pequeños.
sentences.translation: The lioness protects her young.

notes: The outside of the ear is oreja. oído is also a form of oír (heard).

sentences.text: Tengo agua en los oídos.
sentences.translation: I've got water in my ears.

sentences.text: Mi hermana tiene muy buen oído para la música.
sentences.translation: My sister has a very good ear for music.

sentences.text: Se acercó y me habló al oído.
sentences.translation: He leaned in and spoke softly in my ear.

sentences.text: De pequeña quería ser científica.
sentences.translation: As a girl, I wanted to be a scientist.

sentences.text: Los científicos han encontrado agua en otro planeta.
sentences.translation: Scientists have found water on another planet.

sentences.text: Un científico habló del problema en la tele.
sentences.translation: A scientist talked about the problem on TV.

sentences.text: Mi trabajo incluye viajar mucho.
sentences.translation: My job includes a lot of travel.

sentences.text: Mis padres siempre me incluyen en sus planes.
sentences.translation: My parents always include me in their plans.

sentences.text: El viaje incluyó una visita al museo.
sentences.translation: The trip included a visit to the museum.

sentences.text: El hotel ofrece actividades para niños.
sentences.translation: The hotel offers activities for children.

sentences.text: ¿Qué actividades hacéis después del colegio?
sentences.translation: What activities do you do after school?

sentences.text: A estas horas hay poca actividad en la oficina.
sentences.translation: At this time of day there's little activity in the office.

sentences.text: A mi hijo le encantan los dragones con alas.
sentences.translation: My son loves dragons with wings.

sentences.text: El príncipe mató al dragón.
sentences.translation: The prince killed the dragon.

sentences.text: En la película, un dragón quema el pueblo.
sentences.translation: In the film, a dragon burns down the village.

sentences.text: Mi generación creció sin internet.
sentences.translation: My generation grew up without the internet.

sentences.text: Tres generaciones viven en esta casa.
sentences.translation: Three generations live in this house.

sentences.text: La generación de mis padres se casó muy joven.
sentences.translation: My parents' generation got married very young.

notes: Works like gustar: me apetece = I feel like it.

sentences.text: ¿Te apetece dar un paseo?
sentences.translation: Do you fancy going for a walk?

sentences.text: Hoy no me apetece salir.
sentences.translation: I don't feel like going out today.

sentences.text: Me apetecía mucho verte.
sentences.translation: I really wanted to see you.

sentences.text: Haz lo que te apetezca.
sentences.translation: Do whatever you feel like.

notes: el capital (masculine) means money for a business.

sentences.text: ¿Cuál es la capital de Portugal?
sentences.translation: What's the capital of Portugal?

sentences.text: Madrid es la capital de España.
sentences.translation: Madrid is the capital of Spain.

sentences.text: Conozco casi todas las capitales de Europa.
sentences.translation: I've been to almost all the capitals in Europe.

sentences.text: Este móvil fue muy barato.
sentences.translation: This phone was really cheap.

sentences.text: La fruta está más barata en el mercado.
sentences.translation: Fruit is cheaper at the market.

sentences.text: Para los niños compro zapatos baratos.
sentences.translation: I buy cheap shoes for the children.

sentences.text: Lo barato sale caro.
sentences.translation: Cheap things cost more in the end.

sentences.text: Mi hermana finge que duerme.
sentences.translation: My sister is pretending to be asleep.

sentences.text: Fingió estar enfermo para no ir al colegio.
sentences.translation: He pretended to be ill so he didn't have to go to school.

sentences.text: Deja de fingir, sé que estás enfadado.
sentences.translation: Stop pretending, I know you're angry.

notes: The same form is used for the plural: los miércoles = on Wednesdays.

sentences.text: La reunión ha pasado al miércoles.
sentences.translation: The meeting has been moved to Wednesday.

sentences.text: Los miércoles mi hijo sale antes del colegio.
sentences.translation: On Wednesdays my son finishes school early.

sentences.text: El miércoles por la noche hay partido.
sentences.translation: There's a match on Wednesday night.

sentences.text: El escritor está terminando su tercera novela.
sentences.translation: The writer is finishing his third novel.

sentences.text: Esta escritora vende millones de libros.
sentences.translation: This writer sells millions of books.

sentences.text: Muchos escritores viven de dar clases.
sentences.translation: Many writers make a living from teaching.

gloss: solitary, keeping to yourself; lonely, deserted (of a place)

sentences.text: Mi vecino es un hombre solitario.
sentences.translation: My neighbour is a man who keeps to himself.

sentences.text: Dimos un paseo por una playa solitaria.
sentences.translation: We went for a walk on a deserted beach.

sentences.text: Fueron unos meses muy solitarios.
sentences.translation: Those were very lonely months.

notes: salto is also 'I jump', from saltar.

sentences.text: El gato subió a la mesa de un salto.
sentences.translation: The cat got onto the table in one jump.

sentences.text: Los niños daban saltos de alegría.
sentences.translation: The children were jumping for joy.

sentences.text: El perro dio un salto y cogió la pelota.
sentences.translation: The dog jumped up and caught the ball.

notes: One single ad is un anuncio.

sentences.text: Trabajo en publicidad.
sentences.translation: I work in advertising.

sentences.text: La publicidad nos hace comprar cosas que no necesitamos.
sentences.translation: Advertising makes us buy things we don't need.

sentences.text: Sin publicidad, nadie conoce tu negocio.
sentences.translation: Without advertising, nobody knows about your business.

notes: As a noun, un temporal is a storm.

sentences.text: Solo me han dado un contrato temporal.
sentences.translation: They've only given me a temporary contract.

sentences.text: El cierre de la tienda es temporal.
sentences.translation: The shop's closure is temporary.

sentences.text: Busco trabajos temporales para el verano.
sentences.translation: I'm looking for temporary jobs for the summer.

gloss: criminal record; history (of an illness in a family)
notes: Mostly plural: tener antecedentes = to have a criminal record.

sentences.text: El sospechoso no tiene antecedentes.
sentences.translation: The suspect has no criminal record.

sentences.text: Tiene antecedentes por robo.
sentences.translation: He has a record for theft.

sentences.text: Hay antecedentes de cáncer en mi familia.
sentences.translation: There's a history of cancer in my family.

sentences.text: El sueldo es atractivo, pero el horario no.
sentences.translation: The salary is attractive, but the hours aren't.

sentences.text: Su forma de hablar la hace atractiva.
sentences.translation: Her way of talking makes her attractive.

sentences.text: Los precios de ese hotel son muy atractivos.
sentences.translation: That hotel's prices are very attractive.

gloss: bar (counter in a café; metal bar); loaf (barra de pan)
notes: In Spain, una barra de pan is a long white loaf.

sentences.text: Comemos en la barra, que es más rápido.
sentences.translation: Let's eat at the bar, it's quicker.

sentences.text: Compra dos barras de pan.
sentences.translation: Buy two loaves of bread.

sentences.text: El ladrón usó una barra de hierro.
sentences.translation: The thief used an iron bar.

sentences.text: Mañana es nuestro aniversario de boda.
sentences.translation: Tomorrow is our wedding anniversary.

sentences.text: Hoy es el aniversario de la muerte de mi abuelo.
sentences.translation: Today is the anniversary of my grandfather's death.

sentences.text: Mis padres pasan sus aniversarios de boda en el mismo restaurante.
sentences.translation: My parents spend their wedding anniversaries at the same restaurant.

sentences.text: Esta noche viene la niñera.
sentences.translation: The babysitter is coming tonight.

sentences.text: Hemos tenido tres niñeras este año.
sentences.translation: We've had three nannies this year.

sentences.text: De joven trabajé de niñera en Londres.
sentences.translation: When I was young, I worked as a nanny in London.

notes: quince días = two weeks.

sentences.text: Mi hermano y yo nos llevamos quince años.
sentences.translation: My brother and I are fifteen years apart.

sentences.text: El autobús pasa cada quince minutos.
sentences.translation: The bus comes every fifteen minutes.

sentences.text: Nos vamos quince días a Italia.
sentences.translation: We're going to Italy for two weeks.

notes: The wall of a room is pared.

sentences.text: Un muro alto rodea el jardín.
sentences.translation: A high wall goes around the garden.

sentences.text: Nos sentamos en el muro del puerto.
sentences.translation: We sat on the harbour wall.

sentences.text: Los muros de la cárcel son muy altos.
sentences.translation: The prison walls are very high.

gloss: to wear, to show off; to shine; to look good

sentences.text: Le encanta lucir su coche nuevo por el barrio.
sentences.translation: He loves showing off his new car around the neighbourhood.

sentences.text: Hoy luce el sol.
sentences.translation: The sun is shining today.

sentences.text: Ese cuadro luce mucho en el salón.
sentences.translation: That painting looks great in the living room.

notes: Irregular: cubierto = covered.

sentences.text: El seguro cubre los daños.
sentences.translation: The insurance covers the damage.

sentences.text: La nieve cubrió el pueblo en una noche.
sentences.translation: Snow covered the village in one night.

sentences.text: La mesa estaba cubierta de papeles.
sentences.translation: The table was covered in papers.

notes: Usually reírse: me río, te ríes, se ríe.

sentences.text: Mi hija se ríe de todo.
sentences.translation: My daughter laughs at everything.

sentences.text: ¿De qué te ríes?
sentences.translation: What are you laughing at?

sentences.text: Su hermano me hace reír.
sentences.translation: Her brother makes me laugh.

sentences.text: Nos reímos mucho con sus historias.
sentences.translation: We laughed a lot at his stories.

sentences.text: Guarda los productos de limpieza lejos de los niños.
sentences.translation: Keep the cleaning products away from the children.

sentences.text: Ese producto ya no se vende.
sentences.translation: That product isn't sold any more.

sentences.text: La empresa ha sacado dos productos nuevos.
sentences.translation: The company has brought out two new products.

notes: Un abrazo is also a friendly way to end a message.

sentences.text: Abrió los brazos y me dio un abrazo.
sentences.translation: He opened his arms and gave me a hug.

sentences.text: Mi abuela da los mejores abrazos.
sentences.translation: My grandmother gives the best hugs.

sentences.text: Nos dimos un abrazo muy fuerte.
sentences.translation: We gave each other a big hug.

notes: Always plural: unas gafas = a pair of glasses.

sentences.text: Me he comprado unas gafas de sol.
sentences.translation: I've bought some sunglasses.

sentences.text: Creo que necesito gafas: no veo bien la tele.
sentences.translation: I think I need glasses: I can't see the TV properly.

sentences.text: Con estas gafas lo veo todo más claro.
sentences.translation: With these glasses I see everything more clearly.

notes: sobrinos can mean nephews and nieces together.

sentences.text: Los hijos de mi hermano son mis sobrinos.
sentences.translation: My brother's children are my nephews and nieces.

sentences.text: Este fin de semana me quedo con mi sobrina.
sentences.translation: This weekend I'm looking after my niece.

sentences.text: Mi sobrino, el hijo de mi hermana, cumple diez años.
sentences.translation: My nephew, my sister's son, is turning ten.

sentences.text: Han puesto una demanda contra la empresa.
sentences.translation: They've filed a lawsuit against the company.

sentences.text: Hay mucha demanda de pisos en el centro.
sentences.translation: There's a lot of demand for flats in the centre.

sentences.text: Este año ha habido varias demandas contra el hospital.
sentences.translation: There have been several lawsuits against the hospital this year.

notes: A finished building is un edificio.

sentences.text: El puente estuvo diez años en construcción.
sentences.translation: The bridge was under construction for ten years.

sentences.text: Mi primo trabaja en la construcción.
sentences.translation: My cousin works in construction.

sentences.text: La construcción del nuevo hospital ya ha empezado.
sentences.translation: Construction of the new hospital has already started.

sentences.text: Las llamadas internacionales son caras.
sentences.translation: International calls are expensive.

sentences.text: Este restaurante tiene fama internacional.
sentences.translation: This restaurant has an international reputation.

sentences.text: Los vuelos internacionales salen de la terminal dos.
sentences.translation: International flights leave from terminal two.

sentences.text: He cambiado la foto de mi perfil.
sentences.translation: I've changed my profile picture.

sentences.text: Su perfil dice que vive en Valencia.
sentences.translation: Her profile says she lives in Valencia.

sentences.text: Ten cuidado con los perfiles falsos.
sentences.translation: Be careful with fake profiles.

sentences.text: Corta la carne en trozos pequeños.
sentences.translation: Cut the meat into small pieces.

sentences.text: Solo he leído un trozo del libro.
sentences.translation: I've only read a bit of the book.

sentences.text: Este trozo de carretera es peligroso.
sentences.translation: This stretch of road is dangerous.

gloss: to repeat, to say again; to have seconds (of food)

sentences.text: Repite conmigo: «buenos días».
sentences.translation: Repeat after me: "good morning".

sentences.text: ¿Puede repetir la pregunta, por favor?
sentences.translation: Could you repeat the question, please?

sentences.text: Mi hijo repitió curso el año pasado.
sentences.translation: My son had to repeat a school year last year.

sentences.text: La sopa estaba tan buena que repetí.
sentences.translation: The soup was so good that I had seconds.

notes: For the area itself, Spanish usually says barrio.

sentences.text: El vecindario hizo una fiesta en la plaza.
sentences.translation: The neighbourhood held a party in the square.

sentences.text: El vecindario está harto de las obras.
sentences.translation: The neighbourhood is fed up with the building work.

sentences.text: Después del incendio, el vecindario ayudó a la familia.
sentences.translation: After the fire, the neighbourhood helped the family.

sentences.text: El precio me parece razonable.
sentences.translation: The price seems reasonable to me.

sentences.text: Sé razonable, es muy tarde para salir.
sentences.translation: Be reasonable, it's very late to go out.

sentences.text: Sus condiciones son razonables.
sentences.translation: Her terms are reasonable.

gloss: manager (of a shop, hotel or business)

sentences.text: Mi hermana es la gerente del hotel.
sentences.translation: My sister is the hotel manager.

sentences.text: El gerente del restaurante nos invitó al postre.
sentences.translation: The restaurant manager gave us dessert on the house.

sentences.text: Hoy hay reunión de gerentes.
sentences.translation: There's a managers' meeting today.

notes: Same form for a man and a woman: el gerente, la gerente. The person who runs a business day to day; the head of a school or a big company is the director.
Not 'sensible': that is sensato.

sentences.text: Mi hijo es muy sensible y llora por todo.
sentences.translation: My son is very sensitive and cries about everything.

sentences.text: Esta crema es para pieles sensibles.
sentences.translation: This cream is for sensitive skin.

sentences.text: Tengo los ojos sensibles a la luz.
sentences.translation: My eyes are sensitive to light.

notes: Feminine: izquierda (la mano izquierda). a la izquierda = on the left.

sentences.text: El corazón está en el lado izquierdo del pecho.
sentences.translation: The heart is on the left side of the chest.

sentences.text: Hoy me he levantado con el pie izquierdo.
sentences.translation: Today I got out of bed on the wrong side.

sentences.text: Tienes el ojo izquierdo un poco rojo.
sentences.translation: Your left eye is a bit red.

sentences.text: Para mí, la personalidad importa más que la cara.
sentences.translation: For me, personality matters more than looks.

sentences.text: Los gemelos se parecen, pero sus personalidades no.
sentences.translation: The twins look alike, but their personalities don't.

sentences.text: Su personalidad cambió después del accidente.
sentences.translation: His personality changed after the accident.

sentences.text: ¿Ya está seca la ropa?
sentences.translation: Is the washing dry yet?

sentences.text: Este año no llueve y el río está seco.
sentences.translation: There's no rain this year and the river is dry.

sentences.text: En otoño el camino está lleno de hojas secas.
sentences.translation: In autumn the path is full of dry leaves.

sentences.text: Duerme tan profundamente que no oye nada.
sentences.translation: She sleeps so soundly that she doesn't hear anything.

sentences.text: Mi abuelo era profundamente religioso.
sentences.translation: My grandfather was deeply religious.

sentences.text: Estoy profundamente agradecida por tu ayuda.
sentences.translation: I'm deeply grateful for your help.

notes: café en grano = coffee beans.

sentences.text: Me ha salido un grano en la nariz.
sentences.translation: I've got a spot on my nose.

sentences.text: No queda ni un grano de arroz.
sentences.translation: There isn't a single grain of rice left.

sentences.text: Le salen granos cuando come chocolate.
sentences.translation: She gets spots when she eats chocolate.

sentences.text: ¿Tienes una moneda de dos euros?
sentences.translation: Do you have a two-euro coin?

sentences.text: Mi hijo guarda las monedas en una caja.
sentences.translation: My son keeps his coins in a box.

sentences.text: ¿Cuál es la moneda de ese país?
sentences.translation: What's the currency in that country?

sentences.text: ¡Ten piedad de nosotros!
sentences.translation: Have mercy on us!

sentences.text: El jefe nos trata sin piedad.
sentences.translation: The boss treats us without mercy.

sentences.text: Pidió piedad al juez.
sentences.translation: He begged the judge for mercy.

sentences.text: Mi marido es ciudadano francés.
sentences.translation: My husband is a French citizen.

sentences.text: Los ciudadanos esperan respuestas del gobierno.
sentences.translation: Citizens are waiting for answers from the government.

sentences.text: Como ciudadana, tengo derecho a saberlo.
sentences.translation: As a citizen, I have a right to know.

gloss: to lock up, to shut in

sentences.text: Mi hijo se encierra en su cuarto toda la tarde.
sentences.translation: My son shuts himself in his room all afternoon.

sentences.text: Encerré al perro en la cocina.
sentences.translation: I shut the dog in the kitchen.

sentences.text: El ladrón estuvo encerrado tres años.
sentences.translation: The thief was locked up for three years.

gloss: to give your opinion, to have an opinion

sentences.text: Todo el mundo opina sobre mi vida.
sentences.translation: Everyone has an opinion about my life.

sentences.text: Prefiero no opinar.
sentences.translation: I'd rather not give my opinion.

sentences.text: Nadie te ha pedido que opines.
sentences.translation: Nobody asked for your opinion.

gloss: edge; rim (of a glass or plate)
notes: In Spain, borde is also slang for rude: ¡Qué borde eres!

sentences.text: No pongas el vaso en el borde de la mesa.
sentences.translation: Don't put the glass on the edge of the table.

sentences.text: La taza está llena hasta el borde.
sentences.translation: The cup is full to the brim.

sentences.text: Esta foto tiene los bordes rotos.
sentences.translation: This photo has torn edges.

sentences.text: La libertad de expresión es un derecho.
sentences.translation: Freedom of expression is a right.

sentences.text: Tenía una expresión de sorpresa en la cara.
sentences.translation: She had a look of surprise on her face.

sentences.text: Estas expresiones solo se usan en España.
sentences.translation: These expressions are only used in Spain.

sentences.text: El escándalo salió en todos los periódicos.
sentences.translation: The scandal was in all the papers.

sentences.text: La prensa vive de los escándalos.
sentences.translation: The press lives off scandals.

sentences.text: Estos precios son un escándalo.
sentences.translation: These prices are outrageous.

notes: tener nervios = to be nervous.

sentences.text: Mañana es la boda y tengo muchos nervios.
sentences.translation: The wedding is tomorrow and I'm really nervous.

sentences.text: El dentista me tocó un nervio.
sentences.translation: The dentist hit a nerve.

sentences.text: Mi abuela tiene nervios de acero.
sentences.translation: My grandmother has nerves of steel.

sentences.text: Desde hoy soy oficialmente abuela.
sentences.translation: As of today, I'm officially a grandmother.

sentences.text: Oficialmente, el problema no existe.
sentences.translation: Officially, the problem doesn't exist.

sentences.text: Ahora sois oficialmente marido y mujer.
sentences.translation: You are now officially husband and wife.

sentences.text: No seas mal perdedor.
sentences.translation: Don't be a bad loser.

sentences.text: El perdedor paga la cena.
sentences.translation: The loser pays for dinner.

sentences.text: En una guerra no hay ganadores, solo perdedores.
sentences.translation: In a war there are no winners, only losers.

sentences.text: El barco puso rumbo al norte.
sentences.translation: The ship set course for the north.

sentences.text: Salimos rumbo al pueblo a las ocho.
sentences.translation: We set off for the village at eight.

sentences.text: Ese chico va sin rumbo por la vida.
sentences.translation: That boy is drifting through life with no direction.

sentences.text: Para comprar pan, hay que bajar al valle.
sentences.translation: To buy bread, you have to go down to the valley.

sentences.text: Un río pasa por el centro del valle.
sentences.translation: A river runs through the middle of the valley.

sentences.text: En invierno, la niebla cubre los valles.
sentences.translation: In winter, fog covers the valleys.

sentences.text: En mi juventud hacía mucho deporte.
sentences.translation: In my youth, I did a lot of sport.

sentences.text: Casi toda la juventud del pueblo se va a la ciudad.
sentences.translation: Almost all the young people in the village leave for the city.

sentences.text: Mi abuela guarda fotos de su juventud.
sentences.translation: My grandmother keeps photos from her youth.

sentences.text: Mi mayor preocupación son mis hijos.
sentences.translation: My biggest worry is my children.

sentences.text: Con tantas preocupaciones, no puedo dormir.
sentences.translation: With so many worries, I can't sleep.

sentences.text: Vi la preocupación en su cara.
sentences.translation: I saw the worry on her face.

sentences.text: El niño va desnudo por la casa.
sentences.translation: The little boy is going around the house naked.

sentences.text: ¡No entres, estoy desnuda!
sentences.translation: Don't come in, I'm naked!

sentences.text: En invierno, los árboles se quedan desnudos.
sentences.translation: In winter, the trees are left bare.

notes: Older spelling: guión.

sentences.text: El director cambió el guion tres veces.
sentences.translation: The director changed the script three times.

sentences.text: Ella escribe los guiones y él dirige las películas.
sentences.translation: She writes the scripts and he directs the films.

sentences.text: El actor no se sabía el guion.
sentences.translation: The actor didn't know his lines.

sentences.text: Llegué a España en mayo.
sentences.translation: I came to Spain in May.

sentences.text: El uno de mayo es fiesta.
sentences.translation: The first of May is a public holiday.

sentences.text: Mayo viene después de abril.
sentences.translation: May comes after April.

notes: The same form is used for the plural.

sentences.text: Hubo caos en el aeropuerto por la tormenta.
sentences.translation: There was chaos at the airport because of the storm.

sentences.text: Con tanto caos, nadie sabía qué hacer.
sentences.translation: With so much chaos, nobody knew what to do.

sentences.text: Con cuatro niños, en casa siempre hay caos.
sentences.translation: With four kids, there's always chaos at home.

sentences.text: El tren es una buena alternativa al avión.
sentences.translation: The train is a good alternative to flying.

sentences.text: Tenemos que buscar alternativas.
sentences.translation: We need to look for alternatives.

sentences.text: Las alternativas a la carne son cada vez más populares.
sentences.translation: Alternatives to meat are more and more popular.

sentences.text: Conducir así fue una estupidez.
sentences.translation: Driving like that was a stupid thing to do.

sentences.text: Contra la estupidez humana no hay nada que hacer.
sentences.translation: There's nothing you can do against human stupidity.

sentences.text: Por culpa de sus estupideces, perdió el trabajo.
sentences.translation: Because of his stupid behaviour, he lost his job.

sentences.text: Lo sorprendente es que nadie se dio cuenta.
sentences.translation: The surprising thing is that nobody noticed.

sentences.text: La película tiene un final sorprendente.
sentences.translation: The film has a surprising ending.

sentences.text: Sus notas este año han sido sorprendentes.
sentences.translation: His marks this year have been surprising.

notes: The same form is used for men and women.

sentences.text: Perdona, he sido un poco egoísta.
sentences.translation: Sorry, I've been a bit selfish.

sentences.text: Es egoísta pensar solo en ti.
sentences.translation: It's selfish to think only about yourself.

sentences.text: Mis compañeros de piso son muy egoístas.
sentences.translation: My flatmates are really selfish.

gloss: truly (a bit more formal than realmente)

sentences.text: Me sentí verdaderamente feliz.
sentences.translation: I felt truly happy.

sentences.text: Su padre era un hombre verdaderamente bueno.
sentences.translation: Her father was a truly good man.

sentences.text: Pocas personas son verdaderamente libres.
sentences.translation: Few people are truly free.
